s1.syndrome_frame: Crusty skin lesion with prolonged duration and irregular shape, with evidence of skin infiltration and variable response to treatment
salient_findings: Irregularly shaped 5 × 3 cm plaque with multiple superficial crusts
Eosinophilic keratinocytes with pleomorphic nuclei and prominent nucleoli infiltrating the reticular dermis
Marked regression of the plaque after treatment, but with residual papular lesions
key_facts: 59-year-old man with a crusty lesion in the right fronto-orbital region
Lesion present for several months
No significant past medical history
Excisional biopsy showed lobules and detached aggregates of eosinophilic keratinocytes
Pleomorphic nuclei and prominent nucleoli infiltrating the reticular dermis
Treatment with cemiplimab 350 mg every 3 weeks
Initial PET/CT showed focal area of uptake in the supraorbital lesion
Follow-up PET/CT showed decreased uptake in the original lesion
Dermoscopic evaluation of residual papules revealed features typical of basal cell carcinoma

shortlist.label: Basal cell carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Dermoscopic evaluation of residual papules revealed features typical of basal cell carcinoma

shortlist.label: Invasive squamous cell carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Excisional biopsy showed lobules and detached aggregates of eosinophilic keratinocytes with pleomorphic nuclei and prominent nucleoli infiltrating the reticular dermis

shortlist.label: Basosquamous carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical presentation and treatment response suggest possibility of dual squamous and basal cell carcinoma components

shortlist.label: Squamous cell carcinoma in situ
shortlist.why_kept: Initial biopsy showed features of squamous cell carcinoma, although invasive component was noted

shortlist.label: Microcystic adnexal carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Irregularly shaped plaque with multiple superficial crusts and dermal infiltration could be consistent with this rare skin malignancy

raw.rationale: The presence of both basal cell carcinoma features in residual papules and initial diagnosis of invasive squamous cell carcinoma suggests a hybrid tumor, which is consistent with basosquamous carcinoma.

rejected.label: Basal cell carcinoma
rejected.why: Does not explain the initial diagnosis of invasive squamous cell carcinoma

rejected.label: Invasive squamous cell carcinoma
rejected.why: Does not account for the basal cell carcinoma features in residual papules

rejected.label: Squamous cell carcinoma in situ
rejected.why: The tumor has already invaded the reticular dermis, indicating invasive disease

rejected.label: Microcystic adnexal carcinoma
rejected.why: The clinical and histological features do not match this rare tumor type
